articles.title: Could vitamin B12 help treat Verheij syndrome? Study finds promising clues

Understanding how nutrients like B12 interact with this process could lead to new dietary or medical interventions for rare diseases.

story.so_far: Medical research into rare genetic conditions like Verheij syndrome often involves studying how basic biological processes, like gene regulation and nutrition metabolism, go wrong at the molecular level.

articles.title: Singapore, Germany test cross-border payments to reduce settlement risk
articles.summary: Singapore and Germany are collaborating to test cross-border payment systems aimed at reducing the risks associated with settling international transactions.
articles.explain: Cross-border payments are transfers of funds between parties in different countries. Settlement risk occurs when there is a delay between the payment being sent and the asset being received, creating a window where one party could theoretically lose their money. This initiative matters because improving these systems reduces costs and transaction times for global businesses.

story.title: Cross-Border Payment Innovation
story.so_far: International financial transactions often face 'settlement risk,' the danger that one party fails to deliver assets after the other has already transferred payment. Central banks and financial hubs are increasingly exploring blockchain and digital payment technologies to make these processes faster, more secure, and less dependent on traditional correspondent banking networks.

timeline.text: Singapore and Germany have initiated joint testing of a new cross-border payment mechanism to mitigate settlement risks.

articles.summary: Berkshire Hathaway has adjusted its portfolio, reducing stakes in financial firms while increasing positions in airline and retail stocks.

By shifting from banks to airlines and retail, Berkshire is indicating a tactical change in its view on which industries might perform better in the coming months. This is a normal part of institutional investment strategy.

story.title: Berkshire Hathaway Portfolio Rebalancing

articles.title: US dollar hits 19-month peak on Fed hike bets; Aussie dips
articles.summary: The US dollar reached a 19-month high due to growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy following strong inflation data.
articles.explain: When traders expect a central bank like the US Federal Reserve (the Fed) to raise interest rates, the currency typically gets stronger because investors get a higher return on assets held in that currency. 'Tightening' refers to the Fed raising rates to cool down the economy and lower inflation. This affects the global economy because many goods and debts are priced in dollars.

articles.title: Oil slips on supply surplus outlook despite Gulf tensions
articles.summary: Oil prices are falling as analysts predict a surplus in global supply despite ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
articles.explain: A 'supply surplus' happens when there is more oil being produced than the world's economy currently needs. Even with threats of conflict, if the market believes there is plenty of oil in storage or being pumped elsewhere, the price will decrease. This is important because lower oil prices often help lower inflation for energy-consuming nations.

story.title: Global Energy Market Surplus
story.so_far: Oil prices are highly sensitive to both supply chain disruptions and general economic demand. Normally, conflict in oil-producing regions leads to price spikes; however, if overall production capacity in other regions outpaces consumer demand, prices will drop regardless of regional tensions.

timeline.text: The International Energy Agency has forecast an oversupply of oil, causing prices to dip despite concerns over regional conflicts in the Gulf.

articles.title: Gold hovers near over one-year low as firm dollar, Fed-hike bets weigh
articles.summary: Gold prices remain near a one-year low, hurt by a strong dollar and the anticipation of higher US interest rates.
articles.explain: Gold is often seen as a 'safe haven' or a hedge against instability. However, because gold does not pay interest or dividends, its value often drops when interest rates rise; investors prefer holding cash or bonds that pay regular interest instead. This creates an inverse relationship between gold prices and the attractiveness of the US dollar.

articles.title: Hackers inject credit card, crypto-stealing malware into 178 major websites
articles.summary: Security researchers found malware on 178 websites designed to steal credit card information and cryptocurrency from visitors.
articles.explain: Malware is malicious software designed to harm computers or steal data. In this incident, hackers targeted specific websites that many people trust to perform transactions. This matters because it illustrates the risks of using digital services where the underlying infrastructure might be vulnerable, leading to financial loss for unsuspecting users.

story.title: Website Supply Chain Security
story.so_far: Cybersecurity threats against financial platforms have increased as digital asset ownership grows. 'Supply chain' attacks in this context occur when hackers compromise the systems or third-party code that a website uses, allowing them to infect legitimate sites and steal user data without the business owner knowing initially.

timeline.text: Major websites, including crypto-related platforms like Ledger and Coinpass, were compromised to distribute malicious scripts.
